newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks mixed,dollar up on rate prospects.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks mixed,dollar up on rate prospects.

text.p: European stocks began the week in a mixed mood on Monday on worries that the United States would raise interest rates for the first time in two years -- a prospect that made the dollar climb.

London, Europe's biggest's bourse, slipped while Frankfurt and Paris made gains but investors kept a wary eye out for Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee, widely expected to raise rates.
The expectations of higher interest rates squeezed the dollar upwards by nearly a pfennig and half a yen in early trading as traders anticipated a more attractive return on dollar-denominated assets.

London equities suffered the most from the interest rates jitters although markets on both sides of the Atlantic saw volatile trading last week after hints by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.
London's FTSE index of leading shares was down 0.5 percent after ending in the minus column in the last five sessions for a total loss of nearly four percent.
"Whilst this is nothing new -- and I think it's pretty well priced into the market -- I think people are focusing on the chance of more rate increases and a rate increase here," said one dealer.

"There's the worry about U.S. rates and Wall Street and we have our own worries here with the uncertainties of the election in front of us. And everyone knows rates have to go up here too," another said.
In contrast, Frankfurt moved ahead by 0.8 percent as investors shrugged off the interest rates worries and instead took comfort from the stronger dollar, seen as good news for the exporting sector.
"The market is suprisingly strong this morning. .. the main factor is that the market has factored in a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," said a Frankfurt trader.

As bourse trade in Frankfurt opened, the focus was on Thyssen AG, which was up 19 marks, or 4.86 percent at 410 marks, rising on reports it was planning to tell shareholders that its shares have the potential to reach a price of around 550 marks.
Last week Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch announced a takeover bid. Since then Thyssen has agreed to discuss a joint steel company. If the talks fail, Krupp said it planned to reinstate the offer.
In Paris, shares climbed at the opening, with the market drawing support from the firm dollar and strong bond markets, traders said.
Among individual stocks, Lyonnaise des Eaux rose 2.67 percent to 576 francs and Suez was up 2.4 percent at 287.10 following newspaper reports the two were preparing a merger.
On the currency front, the dollar began European trade on a strong note with analysts also predicting a 25 basis point hike in the key Fed funds rate at Tuesday's FOMC meeting.

"A 25 basis point hike has already been priced in... The increase we're looking for tomorrow would be seen as the first of a number of increases," said Julian Fisher, international economist at Daiwa Europe in London.

"People say it (the rate hike) has been discounted by the market, but when the Fed finally actually moves, spot interest rate diffentials will widen and that obviously is supportive for the dollar," said Mark Hendriks, international econoimst at SBC Warburg.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6907 marks and 122.98 yen compared with 1.6835 marks and 122.55 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 29.2 points at 4,225.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 4.58 points at 2,591.71.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 23.71 points at 3,321.95.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $351.35 an ounce, against London's close of $352.65 on Friday. Silver was at $5.15, down three cents.
